title: Spaghetti Puttanesca with Tuna
changes_from_base: Flaked tinned tuna folded in off the heat; shallot and fried tomato purée added to the base; fewer anchovies.
summary: This follows the classic spaghetti puttanesca method, but uses fewer anchovies, adds shallot and fried tomato purée to the base, and folds in flaked tinned tuna off the heat at the end.
equipment: large frying pan or sauté pan (30 cm)

ingredients.item: fine salt for 3 litres of pasta water (0.5%)
ingredients.note: about 2.5 tsp; most of it goes down the drain

ingredients.item: tinned whole plum tomatoes (2 tins), crushed by hand
tinned tuna in olive oil, drained and flaked

steps.title: Boil the pasta water
steps.text: Bring 3 litres of water to the boil with only the 15 g of salt, since the anchovies, capers, olives and tuna all bring their own saltiness. Keep it at a simmer, covered, until the sauce is under way; the pasta goes in during step 4.

steps.title: Build the base
steps.text: Put the oil, garlic, shallot, anchovies, capers, olives and chilli flakes into the cold pan and bring to a sizzle over medium-high heat. Turn the heat down to medium-low and cook for 5-6 minutes, until the shallot has softened and the garlic is lightly golden.

steps.title: Fry the tomato purée
steps.text: Stir in the tomato purée and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring often, until it darkens slightly. Frying the purée directly in the hot oil caramelises its sugars, giving the sauce a deeper flavour than if it were added straight into the liquid.

steps.title: Simmer the sauce
steps.text: Add the crushed tomatoes and simmer gently for 15 minutes, breaking up the larger pieces with a spoon as they soften. You're after a thick, chunky sauce that clings to the pasta rather than a thin one that runs off it. When the sauce has about 10 minutes left, bring the water back to a rolling boil, add the spaghetti or linguine, stir during the first minute, and cook for 2 minutes less than the packet time.

steps.title: Drain the pasta
steps.text: Reserve 240 ml of the pasta cooking water, then drain the pasta.

steps.title: Toss the pasta in the sauce
steps.text: Add the drained pasta and 60 ml of the reserved water to the sauce and toss over medium heat for 1-2 minutes, until the pasta is al dente and well coated. Add a little more water if the sauce gets too thick.

steps.title: Fold in the tuna and serve
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat, then gently fold in the flaked tuna, in large pieces, and the parsley. Adding the tuna off the heat at the very end keeps it moist instead of dry and stringy. Taste before adding any extra salt, as the sauce is already well seasoned, then serve straight away.

tips: Hold back on extra salt until you taste at the end - anchovies, capers, olives and tuna already season the sauce generously.
Fold the tuna in off the heat at the very last minute; cooking it further turns it dry and stringy.
Fry the tomato purée until it darkens slightly before adding the tinned tomatoes - skipping this leaves the sauce tasting flat.
Keep back the reserved pasta water; a splash at the end helps the sauce coat the strands instead of sitting in a puddle.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a pan with a splash of water, stirring, until piping hot throughout (74°C); freezing isn't recommended as the tuna's texture suffers on thawing. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
